newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks reverse gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks reverse gains on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks gave back early gains and ended lower Thursday for the first time since Nov. 4 as investors took profits, traders said.
"Heavyweights like Telmex and Femsa hauled us up in the morning, and profit-takers stepped in later. After the recent run of gains, it had to happen," one trader said.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 8.74 points at 3,392.22. Volume was a moderate 85.9 million shares traded.
In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 54 to 37.
Analysts said stocks could resume their climb, though the direction was unlikely to be straight up.
"We see 3,500 as being a short-term target, although some churning on the way would be natural," said Daniel Romo, research manager at the Bancrecer financial group.
Romo noted political controversy but said it was not hurting the market, referring to ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party deputies' reluctance to vote on a political reform bill before Congress.
"Dealers are beginning to digest the budget. This is a bull market, and we expect to see the year end at 3,700-3,750 points," he added.
Phone company Telmex L series ended up four centavos ($0.01) at 12.64 pesos ($1.60). Holding company Femsa ended down 30 centavos ($0.04) at 26.80 pesos ($3.39).
Financial stock Serfin led the gainers, up 23 centavos ($0.03) at 3.70 pesos ($0.47) as it recovered some ground but remained well off its year high of 6.24 pesos ($0.79).
Another financial stock, BBVPro, headed the losers, off four centavos ($0.01) at 41 centavos ($0.05).
Several other financial stocks ended down, and traders noted that the banks' past-due loans problem was a cause for concern.
